activities.name: The All-Day Open Call ("I'll Be Here, Dip In")
activities.one_liner: An open FaceTime call left running for hours while one partner has a full free day and the other works, with zero obligation to talk — a low-attention presence line either can dip into.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call in the morning on the free partner's day off and prop the phone on a stand rather than holding it
The free partner goes about errands, hobbies, or chores with the call open; the working partner keeps it minimized/muted on their desk
Agree in advance there is no obligation to narrate constantly — comfortable silence is the point, glance over and talk during natural breaks
Plug in to power for calls running longer than roughly 2 hours — continuous FaceTime is heavy on battery and can cause the phone to overheat
Either partner can end and restart the call without it being a signal of anything; treat it as resumable, not a single unbroken session
activities.timezone_friction: This is the direct answer to W8/W9 — the one day each week where one partner has zero work obligations and the other is fully occupied. It only works because it demands nothing continuous from the working partner; it would fail in W4 (hard 60-min stop) or W1 (she needs to actually sleep, not half-listen).

activities.name: Persistent Two-Person Discord Voice Room
activities.one_liner: A private Discord server with a single always-open voice channel that either partner can join or leave anytime without calling, ringing, or scheduling.
how_it_works: Create a small private Discord server with just the two of them and one voice channel that stays there permanently
Whoever is free joins the channel — no invite or ring needed, the other simply sees them join
Leave video off by default to save battery/bandwidth; turn the camera on only when actually chatting
Use the server's text channel to drop a note ("stepping out, back in 20") without breaking the ambient thread
This survives for days at a time since nobody has to actively "answer" a call — you just click in or out
activities.timezone_friction: Discord voice channels have no calling/ringing step, which is exactly what W8/W9 need — the free partner can join and leave without ever interrupting the working partner's day. Works less well for W1 because Discord isn't optimized for in-bed, screen-off use the way FaceTime propped on a stand is.

activities.name: Silent Co-Working Block (DIY Focusmate Rules)
activities.one_liner: A scheduled silent work session over FaceTime borrowing Focusmate's exact structure — declare your task, camera on, no talking during the block, check in at the end — run privately between the two of them instead of with a stranger.
how_it_works: Pick a 25, 50, or 75-minute block (Focusmate's standard durations) and start a FaceTime call at the agreed time
Each says out loud what they're working on in the first 10-30 seconds, matching Focusmate's own session opening
Keep video on and visible for the whole block; audio can be muted if one is also on a separate work call — Focusmate's rules explicitly allow muting audio while keeping video on
Work in silence, no chat, for the full block — talking is reserved for the beginning and end
At the end, unmute and check in for a minute on how it went before hanging up or rolling into another block
activities.timezone_friction: Note: real Focusmate does not let you pick your own partner from the start — it randomly matches you with a stranger, so it cannot reliably pair the two of them together (confirmed via Focusmate's own FAQ). This entry borrows Focusmate's rule structure and runs it privately over FaceTime instead. Fits W5 when she is still working while he does his own quiet evening task nearby; fits W8/W9 when the working partner needs to focus and the free partner does their own thing alongside on camera.

activities.name: Scheduled Group Co-Working Session (Flow Club / Caveday)
activities.one_liner: Instead of a private silent block, each partner drops into a scheduled group virtual coworking session with guided breaks and other participants, then compares notes over FaceTime after.
how_it_works: Sign up for a Flow Club or Caveday session at a time that overlaps their schedules
Join individually for a guided 50-90 minute focus block with a host and other participants — Caveday adds structured breaks and a live guide, Flow Club is closer to open group body doubling
Optionally keep a second device on FaceTime with the partner beside the session, muted, for shared ambient presence
Afterward, hop on FaceTime to debrief what got done
activities.cost: paid (pricing not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Both platforms run continuous session slots throughout the day, so there is very likely an overlapping slot even across the 7-hour gap — but this needs both partners scheduling separately rather than calling each other directly, so it is a secondary variety option to the DIY FaceTime body-doubling entry.

activities.name: Apple Fitness+ Group Workout over SharePlay
activities.one_liner: Start a FaceTime call and launch an Apple Fitness+ workout together via SharePlay — same class, synced playback, each sees the other's effort in real time.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call on iPhone or iPad; both need active Apple Fitness+ subscriptions
Open the Fitness app and start a group workout, or start the workout first and share it into the FaceTime call
The workout plays in sync for both; either partner can control playback (pause, etc.) and it applies to both
Burn Bar and ring-closing notifications let each see the other's effort live during HIIT, Treadmill, Cycling, and Rowing workouts
Works on Apple TV too for a bigger screen while staying connected via FaceTime on iPhone/iPad
activities.cost: paid ($9.99/month, or bundled with Apple One)
activities.timezone_friction: Needs both people genuinely energized, which makes Saturday (W7) the natural home; it can also work in W5 since she's typically post-work energized then, but only tag W5 on days he opts into an earlier slot since he may be too tired late at night.

activities.name: Private Zwift Meetup Ride
activities.one_liner: Set up a private Zwift Meetup so just the two of them ride the same virtual course together in-game, regardless of the real fitness-level gap between them.
how_it_works: Both need a Zwift account/subscription and a trainer (or Zwift's running mode)
Use the Zwift Companion app to create a private Meetup and invite only each other
Zwift's Meetup 'keep everyone together' option keeps riders grouped regardless of power output, so a fitness mismatch doesn't split them apart
Talk over FaceTime audio (phone propped nearby) while riding
Ride the same course simultaneously and watch each other's avatar throughout
activities.timezone_friction: Saturday is the only day both are reliably free and energized enough for a real joint workout, so this is a W7-only entry; the 'kept together' Meetup setting is specifically what makes it work despite differing fitness levels.

activities.name: Run the Same Segment, Compare on Strava
activities.one_liner: Each runs their own route on their own continent and uses Strava's Effort Comparison and Flyby tools to compare pace and splits afterward — no live call required.
how_it_works: Both log runs to Strava; find or create a matching segment and each run it separately, any time, any day
Use Strava's Effort Comparison feature from the activity page to overlay two efforts and see the time gap along the route
Alternatively use the Flyby visual comparison tool for a side-by-side animated view (both need Flyby enabled in privacy settings)
Discuss splits together on the next call — the comparison itself doesn't need to happen live
tools_needed: Strava subscription for full Effort Comparison
activities.timezone_friction: This is asynchronous by design — each runs on their own free day (his Friday, her Sunday) at whatever time suits, and the comparison/conversation happens later. It needs no real-time overlap at all, which is exactly what W8/W9 reward.

activities.name: The Sleep Call
activities.one_liner: A FaceTime call left running while one partner falls asleep and the other stays awake or quietly signs off — the propped-phone version of just being in the room at night.
how_it_works: Start the call when she's winding down for bed, which lands during his midday/lunch (W1)
Prop the phone on a stand rather than holding it, camera angled loosely at the bed rather than a tight face shot
Dim screen brightness low, both to reduce eye strain and to cut heat/battery drain during a long call
Turn on Do Not Disturb on both ends so nothing interrupts once she's settled
Agree in advance on who ends the call — usually whoever is still awake once breathing has clearly settled — rather than leaving it ambiguous

Plug the phone in to charge if the call is expected to run over an hour; continuous FaceTime is one of the more battery- and heat-intensive things a phone does. In the specific 7-hour-gap version, he wakes into his day still on the call while she is genuinely asleep on her end — treat that as the expected, not accidental, outcome
activities.timezone_friction: W1 is exactly his fresh-morning / her sleepy-night overlap — he can stay lightly present while getting ready for his day as she drifts off, which is the asymmetry this window is built around. Doesn't substitute for W6 — falling asleep on a call is not the 'event-grade' use of that rarer, costlier window.

activities.name: Narrate Your Day While She Lies in the Dark
activities.one_liner: Rather than shared silence, one partner actively talks through the details of their day — audio only, eyes-closed on the listening end — while the other winds down toward sleep.
how_it_works: Time this for W1: he's just finished something (a workout, a walk, breakfast) and calls while she's already in bed with the lights off
She doesn't need to hold the phone or watch the screen — audio only, propped or on speaker
He narrates in loose real time rather than a tidy recap: what he's looking at, what he's about to do, small sensory detail rather than a plain list of facts
She can respond minimally or not at all — the format doesn't require reciprocity, which is what makes it work when she's nearly asleep
End when she stops responding or audibly drifts off
activities.timezone_friction: This exploits the W1 asymmetry directly rather than tolerating it: he's fresh and talkative, she's fading and doesn't need to perform engagement back. It would not work in W5/W6, where the energy roles reverse and reading real fatigue cues matters.

activities.name: Guided Walking Tour of His Neighbourhood
activities.one_liner: He walks his usual route with the phone camera facing outward — not selfie mode — narrating what she'd see if she were there, while she watches from a desk with no ability to move.
how_it_works: Flip the phone camera from the selfie/portrait view to the rear-facing view, so she sees what he sees instead of his face — a technique documented in professional virtual walkthrough guidance
He walks a real route — to a café, the beach, a market — at a normal pace, narrating like a tour guide: what's around the corner, a smell, a shop he likes
She stays passive, watching and asking questions rather than doing anything herself
Works especially well when she's stuck at a desk (W4) or still in bed (W1/W2) and physically can't be anywhere but where she is
activities.timezone_friction: The rear-camera 'reveal the surroundings, not your face' technique is documented for virtual walkthroughs generally, not for LDR couples specifically — this entry is a synthesis of that verified mechanic applied to the brief's explicit request for a narrated-walk pattern. It exploits the walking/stationary asymmetry directly: he moves, she watches, fitting whichever window has him mobile and her fixed in place.

activities.name: Same Recipe, Different Kitchens
activities.one_liner: Pick one recipe both can make with what's in their own kitchens, prep separately, then cook it together in real time over video, timing steps to match.
how_it_works: Agree on a recipe in advance that both can source locally — avoid anything needing an ingredient only available in one country
Each preps their own ingredients (mise en place) before the call so cook times stay roughly matched
Start the FaceTime call and prop the phone so both hands are free
Narrate steps out loud as you go so timing stays roughly in sync even without a shared timer
Sit down and eat 'together' on camera at the end, phone propped facing the food and faces rather than held
activities.timezone_friction: Saturday (W7) is the only slot where both are reliably free long enough for a full cook-plus-eat session without a hard stop; a shorter version exists for W4/W2 (see 'One Cooks, One Reads the Recipe Aloud') since a full from-scratch cook doesn't fit inside her 60-minute lunch.

activities.name: His Dinner, Her Lunch
activities.one_liner: A short, no-pressure 'eat together' window that exploits the meal-time overlap created by the 7-hour gap — his evening meal lands during her workday lunch, his lunch lands near her breakfast.
how_it_works: Check the day's overlap: his ~18:00-19:00 dinner (IL) lines up with her ~11:00-12:00 lunch (NYC) — that's W4; his ~12:00-13:00 lunch lines up with her ~5:00-6:00am, relevant only if she's up (W2)
Start a short FaceTime call timed to whichever meal overlap is live that day
Prop the phone facing the food and faces rather than holding it, so both hands stay free to eat
Keep it conversational and bounded — no obligation to finish the whole meal on camera, especially for her hard-stop lunch break
Each just eats what they already have — this doesn't require ordering food across borders
activities.timezone_friction: This is the direct answer to the W4/W2 co-eating ask: the meal overlap exists automatically because of the 7-hour gap, not despite it. Cross-border food delivery does NOT work as a shortcut here — Wolt's own Israel terms require an Israeli-issued credit card and require the person placing the order to be physically located in Israel, so she cannot order food to his address (or vice versa) from abroad; each eating their own already-available food sidesteps the problem entirely.

activities.name: Reading Aloud Until She Sleeps
activities.one_liner: One partner reads a single shared novel aloud over the call at bedtime — not each reading separately, one book, one voice — continuing a chapter or two at a time across sessions.
how_it_works: Pick one book (fiction works best) that only one of you needs a physical or e-book copy of — the other just listens
Call at her bedtime (W1) and read for as long as attention holds, typically a chapter
Switch to audio-only or screen-off partway through as she gets sleepier, so she doesn't need to keep watching video
Pick up at the same bookmark next session — this is explicitly a multi-week continuity ritual, not a one-off
The listening partner doesn't need to hold the phone once settled — prop it or switch to a voice call
activities.timezone_friction: W1 only — this is specifically a falling-asleep ritual and depends on one partner being genuinely sleepy and passive, which only happens in her wind-down window.

activities.name: Getting Ready Together on Speaker
activities.one_liner: A low-attention audio call run in the background while each does their own getting-ready routine — brushing teeth, making coffee, dressing — with occasional check-ins, no dedicated attention required.
how_it_works: Call at a moment both are getting ready — for her that's early morning before her commute (W3), or if she's an early riser, meeting his midday (W2)
Put the phone on speaker and set it down rather than holding it, so both hands stay free
There's no obligation to maintain eye contact or even constant talk — comment on what you're doing, ask what's on the calendar, go quiet while brushing teeth
This is audio-first and screen-optional, which matters because she may be moving around getting dressed, not looking at a screen
activities.timezone_friction: This is one of the only entries that genuinely fits W3's hard constraint — audio-only, hands-busy, no screen required at all, since it runs on speakerphone rather than FaceTime video. It also works in W2 (his lunch, her dawn) if she's an early riser.

activities.name: Walk-and-Talk Commute Call
activities.one_liner: A pure audio call for her commute — he talks in her ear through headphones while she walks or rides transit, hands and eyes free for navigating.
how_it_works: Call (a regular phone call or audio-only FaceTime) right as she leaves for her commute, W3
She wears headphones so both hands stay free for a bag, coffee, or a subway pole
Keep the conversation low-stakes and interruptible — she may need to pause for a crosswalk, a ticket gate, or a loud subway car
He can talk while walking his own errand on his end too, making it doubly mobile if he chooses
End naturally when she arrives, no formal goodbye required
activities.timezone_friction: This is the single most direct fit for W3's constraint (mobile, hands busy, no screen) — audio-only and interruptible by design. It cannot extend to W4 because her lunch has a hard stop and a desk/public setting a walking commute call doesn't share.

activities.name: Parallel Play: Read/Craft/Scroll Side by Side
activities.one_liner: A short evening version of ambient co-presence — each does their own unrelated activity (a book, a craft, scrolling) on an open call, camera on, without pressure to interact constantly.
how_it_works: Open a FaceTime call in the evening with no planned activity
Each picks something solo — a book, a sketchbook, a show only one of you wants to watch, phone scrolling
Keep cameras on so you're visibly present to each other, similar to sharing a physical room
Talk when something comes up, otherwise let comfortable silence run — this is the point, not a failure state
activities.timezone_friction: Good for W5 when he's tired and doesn't have energy for a structured activity but still wants presence; a lighter version also works for W1 as an alternative to the sleep call when she's not quite ready to drop off yet.

activities.name: One Cooks, One Reads the Recipe Aloud
activities.one_liner: Instead of both cooking, only one is actually in the kitchen — the other reads the recipe aloud step by step and keeps them company, with no ingredients or kitchen needed on their end.
how_it_works: The cooking partner picks a recipe and shares the source (screenshot, link, or just tells the other) before the call
Call starts once they're in the kitchen with ingredients out
The non-cooking partner reads each step aloud as the other works, holding pace with what's happening rather than reading ahead
The non-cooking partner does nothing else demanding — this can run from a desk, a couch, even a commute if it's audio-only
Ends when the dish is done — the cook eats; the reader has already eaten or eats separately
activities.timezone_friction: This sidesteps the matched-ingredients problem of full two-kitchen cooking ('Same Recipe, Different Kitchens') and needs nothing from the non-cooking partner, so it fits inside her hard 60-minute lunch stop (W4) or his lunch/her dawn (W2) far more easily than a full cook-along.

activities.name: Bedtime Yoga Wind-Down Together
activities.one_liner: Both do the same short, named bedtime yoga video as a physical wind-down before the sleep call, camera propped to show the mat rather than the face.
how_it_works: Pick a specific bedtime yoga video from Yoga With Adriene's channel — the 7-Minute Bedtime Yoga or the 12-Minute Wind Down sequence are both named, repeatable options
Start a FaceTime call, then both hit play on the same YouTube video on a count of three so they move roughly together
Prop the phone to show the mat/body rather than a tight face shot, similar to the sleep-call framing
Talk is minimal during the practice — Adriene narrates the poses for both
Roll straight from the mat into the sleep call once finished, since this is designed as a pre-bed wind-down, not a workout
activities.timezone_friction: This is explicitly a low-energy wind-down practice, which fits only her pre-sleep W1 window; he'd do it at an odd hour purely for her sake, which is workable since the practice itself is gentle and short (7-12 min) rather than a real workout, unlike the Fitness+ or Zwift entries.

This is the brief's named top community source and I could not reach it at all. As a direct consequence, the most asymmetry-exploiting entries the brief asked me to prioritize — narrate-day-eyes-closed, getting-ready-together-speakerphone, walk-and-talk-commute, guided-tour-neighbourhood, same-recipe cooking, read-recipe-aloud — are sourced to a single company blog, a single identifiable-author Substack post, a general listicle-adjacent blog, or an adjacent-domain official document, and are marked confidence: low or medium rather than high. None are invented; each has a real, opened URL, but the sourcing tier is weaker than the brief's stated priority order for this territory.

Could not verify whether 'Around' (the ambient floating-head video app) is still operating in 2026 — all sources found were 2020-era TechCrunch/Computerworld coverage. Left out of the final activity list rather than included with stale sourcing; worth a follow-up check before the library ships.

Meal-kit shipping to Israel (HelloFresh specifically) returned conflicting signals: an Israeli App Store listing exists, but Israel is not listed among HelloFresh's stated direct operating countries in the sources found. Left as UNKNOWN. The two cooking entries both route around this by having each partner buy their own local groceries rather than relying on a shipped kit, so the library doesn't depend on this being resolved.

Wolt's cross-border ordering restriction (Israeli card + orderer physically in Israel required) was verified directly from Wolt's own Terms of Use, but I did not check whether other Israeli delivery services (10bis, Cibus, Mishlox) have different rules — flagged as a further-research item, not assumed to be universal.

Apple Watch Walkie-Talkie (official Apple feature, verified) was considered for quick W3/W8/W9 touches but not built into a full activity entry, since the brief only confirms both partners are on 'Apple devices' with FaceTime, not that both own Apple Watches specifically.

The Bedtime Window academic research project (Newcastle University OpenLab / Microsoft Research / Monash) is a real, verified research prototype on ambient bedtime presence for LDR couples, but it is not a shippable consumer product the couple can actually use — I used it only as supporting design rationale for the sleep-call entry's timezone_friction reasoning, not as a standalone activity, to avoid recommending something unavailable to them.

I did not independently verify current pricing for Flow Club or Caveday subscriptions; cost field is marked paid with an explicit 'pricing not independently verified' note rather than a specific figure.
confidence_summary: MEDIUM. Core mechanics for named products/services (Focusmate, Discord, Apple Fitness+, Zwift, Strava, Wolt's Israel terms, Yoga With Adriene) are HIGH confidence, verified directly from official vendor documentation. The entries the brief most wanted — the asymmetry-exploiting narration and mobile/hands-busy patterns for W1/W3/W4 — are the weakest-sourced because reddit.com was completely unreachable for this entire research session (both search and direct fetch), which was the brief's top community source for exactly this kind of granular, real-couple ritual. Those entries are honestly marked confidence: low or medium and each still carries one real, opened source rather than an invented one.
thin_window_note: Served all five thin windows. W8/W9 (my primary ownership per the dispatch) got the strongest coverage and the best sourcing: all-day open FaceTime call, persistent Discord voice room, DIY body-doubling block, and asynchronous Strava effort comparison — all anchored in official product documentation. W2/W3/W4 got real coverage too (getting-ready-on-speaker, walk-and-talk commute, guided neighbourhood tour, his-dinner-her-lunch, read-recipe-aloud) with at least two entries (getting-ready-speakerphone, walk-and-talk-commute) meeting the strict audio-only/hands-busy/no-screen constraint, but these are exactly the entries where sourcing is weakest, for the reason detailed in gaps: reddit.com was unreachable for the entire session, both via WebSearch site: queries and direct WebFetch (reddit.com, old.reddit.com, and the reddit JSON search endpoint all failed), so the brief's top community source for this territory could not be used at all. I did not fabricate replacements — each thin-window entry still has one real, opened, non-Reddit source, but confidence is honestly capped at low/medium for most of them.
